buckets.root_cause: spurious:E008_return_unit + spurious:E170_effect_row — ONE bridge-state bug (front-half by-value bridge drops the declared return type to () and drops the effect row, so value-returning fns get E008 and .value access gets E170)
buckets.root_cause_detail: The *mut by-value bridge in check.sio (around check.sio:1146 / the `return` at ~2489) loses the FnSig return type and effect row when crossing the by-value leaf, so every value-returning fn is type-checked as if it returns () and every Knowledge.value read is checked as if `with Epistemic` is absent. ~96 programs have this as their SOLE blocker; ~36 more emit it as noise alongside a genuine error.
buckets.likely_fix: Carry the declared return type and effect row through the by-value bridge (read FnSig.ret + FnSig.effects via the proven .find/.get path) instead of defaulting to unit/empty at the bridge boundary; fix at check.sio:1146 and the return at ~2489.
buckets.leverage_note: Single highest-leverage fix: clears the sole blocker on ~96 programs and removes noise from ~36 more (~132 touched). This is the largest bucket and one bug.

buckets.root_cause: parse_gap:float_exponent — scientific-notation float literals (1.0e-15, 3.0e-26, 1e-30) are mis-lexed; cascades into expr/block parse errors, especially `<float>e<exp> {` before a brace
buckets.root_cause_detail: The lexer does not accept an exponent suffix on float literals, so `1.0e-30` breaks tokenization; when the literal sits in an `if`/`while` condition just before `{`, it also derails struct-literal-vs-block disambiguation. Spread across parse_gap:float_exponent, parse_gap:float_exponent_literal, and the scientific-notation entries inside parse_gap:other.
buckets.likely_fix: Extend the float lexer to consume `[eE][+-]?[0-9]+` exponent suffixes and re-emit a single float token.
buckets.leverage_note: Largest single REAL (non-spurious) bug: one lexer change unblocks ~54 numeric/PBPK/ODE/algebra programs.

buckets.root_cause: type_error:E004 — integer/float width mismatch (i32 vs i64, f32 vs f64, i64 vs usize) on binary operators; literals default to i64/f64 and won't combine with narrower operands
buckets.root_cause_detail: Numeric literal default typing (i64 / f64) is not unified with the declared narrower operand type, so `i32_var + literal`, `f32 + 0.5`, and `i64 op usize` all fail E004. Genuine checker gap in literal/operand type inference.
buckets.likely_fix: Apply bidirectional literal type inference at binary-op sites: coerce untyped int/float literals to the other operand's concrete width before the combine check.
buckets.leverage_note: Second-largest genuine type bug; one inference fix unblocks ~26 arithmetic/algebra/autodiff programs.

buckets.root_cause: type_error:E014 — array index via `as usize` (and other non-i64 index types) rejected as 'array indices must be integers'
buckets.root_cause_detail: The index type check only accepts i64; `usize` (and `i as usize` casts) are not recognized as integer index types, so idiomatic `arr[i as usize]` fails.
buckets.likely_fix: Treat usize and all integer widths as valid array-index types in the index type check.
buckets.leverage_note: One check.sio predicate change unblocks ~18 buffer/matrix/GPU-style programs.

buckets.root_cause: parse_gap:other — extern "C" { ... } foreign-function blocks (incl. semicolon-terminated and multi-decl/void-return decls) not parsed
buckets.root_cause_detail: The parser does not handle `extern "C" { fn ...; }` declaration blocks: trailing-semicolon decls, second decls, and void-return fns all fail.
buckets.likely_fix: Add an extern-block grammar production accepting `;`-terminated and void-return fn signatures.
buckets.leverage_note: One grammar addition unblocks ~9 FFI/stdlib programs.

buckets.root_cause: parse_gap:kernel_fn — `kernel fn ... with GPU` declarations (and GPU slice args &![f64]) not parsed
buckets.root_cause_detail: The `kernel fn` declaration keyword and its GPU effect/mutable-slice argument forms are unparsed (parse_gap:kernel_fn_decl plus the kernel-fn entries inside parse_gap:other).
buckets.likely_fix: Add `kernel fn` to the item grammar, reusing the normal fn-decl path plus the `with GPU` effect row and `&![T]` slice params.
buckets.leverage_note: One keyword/grammar addition unblocks the entire GPU kernel suite (~15 programs).

buckets.root_cause: parse_gap:refinement_type — refinement types `{ x: T | pred }` in param/return/let/alias positions not parsed
buckets.root_cause_detail: The brace-bar refinement syntax `{ n: i32 | n > 0 }` (in fn params, returns, let bindings, and `type X = { ... }` aliases) is unparsed; spread across parse_gap:type_alias and the refinement entries in parse_gap:other.
buckets.likely_fix: Add a refinement-type production in the type grammar: `{ ident: Type | Expr }`, usable wherever a type is expected.
buckets.leverage_note: One type-grammar production unblocks ~13 refinement/proof programs.

buckets.root_cause: parse_gap:fn_type_param — first-class/function-pointer parameter and return types `fn(T)->T` (incl. `with` effect row) not parsed; checker also silently rejects fn-typed values
buckets.root_cause_detail: `fn(i64)->i64`, `fn(i64)->i64 with IO`, fn-type returns, and named-fn-as-value all fail — some as parse errors (parse_gap:other), some as silent checker rejections classified type_error:other.
buckets.likely_fix: Add fn-type syntax to the type grammar including optional `with <effects>` row, and wire fn-typed values through the checker as first-class.
buckets.leverage_note: One type-grammar + checker change unblocks ~11 HOF/closure-as-value programs.

buckets.root_cause: parse_gap:algebra_decl / study_block — `algebra X over f64 { add:..., basis:... }` and `study { hypothesis ... }` DSL declaration blocks not parsed
buckets.root_cause_detail: Two top-level DSL block forms are unparsed: the `algebra ... over ... { property-lists; basis }` declaration and the `study {...}/hypothesis {...}` research-DSL block (the latter cascades to ~47 errors each).
buckets.likely_fix: Add grammar productions for the algebra declaration and the study/hypothesis block (separate but both top-level item forms).
buckets.leverage_note: ~13 programs (10 algebra + 3 study) over two related grammar additions.

buckets.root_cause: type_error:E001 — unit-typed let bindings (mg, kg, s, J, user `unit`) reject f64 literals; Unobserved<T> binding mismatches
buckets.root_cause_detail: A `let x: mg = 500.0` binding rejects the f64 literal because unit types are not treated as coercion targets for numeric literals; same class covers Unobserved<f64> bindings.
buckets.likely_fix: Allow numeric literals (and their base scalar type) to bind to unit-refined types in the binding-type check.
buckets.leverage_note: One binding-check change unblocks the ~7 unit-type programs plus the 2 Unobserved cases.

buckets.root_cause: parse_gap:const_decl — top-level `const NAME: i64 = N` declarations not parsed (each ontology file has ~20, cascading to ~120 errors)
buckets.root_cause_detail: Top-level `const` item declarations are unparsed; the generated ontology type files are all const-only.
buckets.likely_fix: Add a top-level `const ident: Type = Expr` item production.
buckets.leverage_note: One item production unblocks all 8 generated-ontology programs.

buckets.root_cause: type_error:E011/E013 — Seq<T> method resolution (.push/.get/.set/.len/.count) and Seq subscript `s[i]` not resolved by the modular frontend
buckets.root_cause_detail: The modular checker does not resolve Seq's built-in methods (E011 no method named) nor Seq indexing (E013 indexing requires array type); Seq is not wired as an indexable/method-bearing builtin.
buckets.likely_fix: Register Seq builtin methods and Seq subscript lowering in the checker's method/index resolution.
buckets.leverage_note: One Seq-builtin wiring unblocks ~9 Seq/collection programs.

buckets.root_cause: parse_gap:generics — generic fn type-parameter lists `fn name<T>` / `<T, U>` not parsed
buckets.root_cause_detail: Angle-bracket generic parameter lists on fn declarations are unparsed.
buckets.likely_fix: Add `<TypeParams>` parsing after the fn name.
buckets.leverage_note: One grammar addition unblocks 4 generics programs (and helps the fn-type/turbofish family).

buckets.root_cause: parse_gap:async_spawn — `async {}` / `spawn {}` block expressions, `.await`, tuple-destructure let, channel::<T> turbofish not parsed
buckets.root_cause_detail: The concurrency surface (async/spawn block exprs, .await, `let (a,b) = ...`, channel::<T>()) is unparsed; clustered in parse_gap:other.

buckets.root_cause: parse_gap:closure / type_error:closure — untyped closure params `|x|` not parsed; first-class fn/closure values silently rejected by checker
buckets.root_cause_detail: Untyped closure params (`|x| x+1`) fail to parse (typed `|x: i64|` parses), and named-fn/closure-as-value is rejected with no E-code; overlaps the fn_type_param bucket.
buckets.likely_fix: Infer closure param types from context (allow untyped `|x|`) and accept fn/closure values as first-class in the checker.

buckets.root_cause: type_error:E003 — `cannot modify an immutable binding` (let used where var/Mut needed)
buckets.root_cause_detail: Programs mutate a `let` binding; the checker correctly flags it but these are likely genuine source fixes or a too-strict mutability inference in epistemic/theorem code.

buckets.root_cause: parse_gap:impl_method — inherent `impl T { fn ... }` blocks (and trait-style impls) not parsed

buckets.root_cause: type_error:other — silent checker rejection (no E-code) of mutable-borrow `&!`/`&!Outer` field stores and fn-pointer params taking `&!` args

totals: 352 total: parse_gap ~163 (sci-notation float ~54, kernel fn ~15, refinement ~13, algebra/study ~13, fn-type ~11, async ~10, extern ~9, const ~8, generics 4, impl 3, misc ~18); spurious-bridge ~132 (E008 + E170, one bug); type_error ~80 (E004 ~26, E014 ~18, E001 ~9, Seq E011/E013 ~9, misc ~9, E003 ~4, other ~4); crash 6.
summary: One bug dominates: the front-half by-value bridge state loss (check.sio:1146 / return ~2489) drops both the declared return type (E008 'expected ()') and the effect row (E170 '.value requires with Epistemic'). It is the SOLE blocker on ~96 programs and noise on ~36 more (~132 touched), and it is a single fix owned by front_half_G1 — do this FIRST. Second, one parser/lexer change to accept scientific-notation float exponents (1.0e-30) unblocks ~54 numeric/PBPK/ODE/algebra programs and is the largest REAL (non-spurious) bug. Third tier is two front_half_G1 type-inference fixes — bidirectional literal width unification (E004, ~26) and accepting usize/`as usize` array indices (E014, ~18). After those four fixes (~230 of 352 programs), the rest is a parser long tail of self-contained grammar productions (kernel fn ~15, refinement types ~13, algebra/study DSL ~13, fn-type params ~11, async/spawn ~10, extern blocks ~9, const decls ~8, generics, impl, misc) plus the 6 checker crashers, which are non-leaf expressions (typed closures, deref-match, heterogeneous tuple access) that simply need to be added to the existing *mut expr spine — the same conversion that already landed for match→if-chain leaves.

verified.evidence:
mc.elf --check (ulimit -s 1048576) emitted EXACTLY two spurious errors on the one correct main(), rc=1 (NOT a crash — the bucket claims spurious type errors, and that is what we got):
  error[E170] at 0..125: accessing .value on epistemic type requires `with Epistemic` effect  (despite `with Epistemic` being declared → effect row dropped)
  error[E008] at 119..129 (the `return 0`): return value does not match function's declared return type, expected (), found i64  (despite `-> i32` → return type dropped to unit)
Literal tokens "error[E008]" and "error[E170]" with the bucket's exact messages are printed, so the labels match the bucket (the report_mismatch path carries its own label, not the diagnostics-mod code-8="unterminated_char" mapping).

SINGLE-CAUSE confirmation (the crux of "ONE bridge-state bug"): in check.sio the inplace handler checker_check_fn_item_inplace populates BOTH per-fn fields at ONE site from a single `sig` — line 2498 `(*c).current_return_type = sig.return_type` and line 2499 `(*c).current_effects = sig.effects`. E008 reads `(*c).current_return_type` (line 2602-2603 in the `return <expr>` path); E170 reads `(*c).current_effects`. The by-value bridge checker_check_items_mut (lines 1156-1157, near the claimed 1146) routes through `(*c).check_items(items)` by value, which never runs that handler against `c`, so both fields stay at their constructor init defaults (line 651 ty_unit() / line 653 [0;8]). One dropped state-set, two read sites → two different symptoms, one cause.

This also explains the decoupling seen in the as-is sample runs (which a skeptic would read as two bugs): basic_math.sio (value-returning, NO epistemic, uses `return`) → E008-only; sensitivity_div.sio (`with IO, Epistemic`, `.value`, trailing-expr `0`) → E170-only. The trailing-expr return takes the direct-`sig2` tail check (lines 2509-2513, reads sig2 directly, immune to the dropped current_return_type), so it shows no E008; `return` statements show E008. Different constructs surface different symptoms of the same dropped FnSig state. The bucket's likely_fix naming two locations (1146 and ~2489) is the populate-end and the read-spine of one dataflow, not two bugs.

SCOPE/CAVEATS: (1) I did NOT verify the fix works (carrying ret+effects through the bridge) — that is fix-verification, out of scope; the `true` is scoped to: the minimal repro reproduces spurious E008+E170 on one correct fn, and both trace to a single shared state-set site. (2) The claimed corpus count 132 is NOT verified by one repro — this confirms the MECHANISM and error codes, not the aggregate count.

Reproduces the bucket's claimed behavior, especially the `<float>e<exp> {` before-a-brace symptom: rc=1, `parse error: expected token at line 5:15 expected=184 actual=123` (123 = the `{`). The cascade EOF error at line 10 (expected=185 actual=0) is downstream, not a second cause.

Single-trigger isolation via probes (all stack-capped at 1048576):
- probe_let (`let a: f64 = 1.0e-15`, no brace) -> NO parse error, only an unrelated E008 return-type error. Exponent float parses fine in a let.
- probe_exp_paren (`let b = a < 1.0e-30`, exponent in comparison, no following brace) -> NO parse error, only type errors. Parses fine.
- probe_noexp (`if a < 2.0 {`, plain float before brace) -> NO parse error, only type errors. Plain float before brace parses fine.
- probe_if (`if a < 1.0e-30 {`) -> PARSE ERROR at the `{`.
- probe_eplus (`1.0e30`) and probe_intexp (`1e30`) before brace -> identical parse error; the minus sign is not required, and an int mantissa exponent triggers it too.

All probes converge on exactly ONE trigger: an exponent-bearing float literal immediately followed by `{` (block open). That confirms a single root cause -> single_cause_confirmed=true.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the bucket: the bucket says the literals are "mis-lexed" and the likely_fix is to extend the FLOAT LEXER to consume `[eE][+-]?[0-9]+`. My probes refute that mechanism — `1.0e-15` / `1.0e-30` / `1e-30` already lex and parse as clean single float tokens in let and comparison contexts (otherwise those probes would also fail). The defect is PARSER-SIDE: the brace-disambiguation heuristic (struct-literal-vs-block) after an exponent-bearing float misfires, expecting token 184 but seeing `{` (123). The likely_fix as written is misdirected; the lexer is fine, the parser's `{`-after-exponent-float handling is the bug.

verified.bucket: type_error:E004 — integer/float width mismatch (i32 vs i64, f32 vs f64, i64 vs usize) on binary operators; literals default to i64/f64 and won't combine with narrower operands
verified.evidence: mc.elf --check on the minimal repro exits rc=1 and emits E004 "these types cannot be combined with this operator / expected i32 / found i64" on the `x + 10` binary op, where `x:i32` and the bare literal `10` defaults to i64. This matches the bucket exactly. Cross-variant probing confirms a SINGLE root cause across the bucket's named cases: (A) i32 var + bare int literal -> E004 expected i32/found i64; (B) f32 + 2.0 -> E004 expected f32/found f64; (C) usize + i64 -> E004 expected usize/found i64. All three are the same combine-check requiring exact type identity with no literal-to-other-operand-width coercion — directly supporting the likely_fix (bidirectional literal coercion at binary-op sites). The repro also incidentally raises E008 on `return 0` (0 defaults to i64, body is i32), which is the SAME underlying cause (default-width literal not coerced to declared narrower type), not a second cause. Note: E004 is a broader code that also fires on category mismatches (e.g. string - int -> E004 expected string/found i64); that is a distinct cause sharing the code, but it is outside this bucket's scope, which is explicitly width mismatch. The bucket as scoped is a single root cause.

verified.bucket: type_error:E014 — array index via `as usize` (and other non-i64 index types) rejected as "array indices must be integers"
verified.evidence:
The minimal repro at /tmp/verify_type_error_18.sio reproduces the bucket exactly: `mc.elf --check` (ulimit -s 1048576) emits `error[E014] at 0..102: array indices must be integers` with the matching help/note text ("use an integer type (i8,i32,i64,u8,u32,u64)" / "array indexing requires an integer type"), rc=1. This is the same E014 message seen on the sample tests (gpu_kernel_basic.sio produced ~25 identical E014 errors, all on `arr[i as usize]`).

Single-cause confirmed via discriminating probes:
- `a[i]` with bare `i: i64` (no cast) → NO E014 (clean index).
- `a[i as usize]` → E014.
- `a[i as u32]` → E014.
The sole discriminator is whether the index is a cast expression (`x as <intwidth>`). The index-type check in the checker fails to recognize the type of a cast result as an integer index type, regardless of the concrete width (usize, u32). That is one mechanism, matching the bucket's claim and likely_fix (treat usize/all integer widths as valid array-index types). The claimed count of 18 is consistent: every occurrence is the same `as <width>`-indexed access (the corpus uses `i as usize` pervasively for indexing).

Caveat (not contaminating): each run also emits unrelated E008 "return value does not match function's declared return type" errors. These fire even on the bare-index program (`a[i]`) that has NO E014, so E008 is a separate pre-existing return-type miscompile, orthogonal to the E014 index-type bucket.

verified.repro: /tmp/verify_parse_gap_18.sio — combines pub field, let _, tuple destructure let, struct destructure let, ~ bitwise-not, and if-let. Clean control (fn main(){println}) reaches check: OK rc=0.
verified.evidence: The bucket's BEHAVIOR reproduces (rc=1, "error: parse_failed", multiple "parse error" lines) — these are genuine parser rejections, not crashes or type errors, and a clean control program reaches check: OK rc=0, so the failures are attributable to the listed syntax features. HOWEVER the claimed SINGLE root cause is FALSE. Each listed feature fails at its own distinct source location with its own distinct expected/actual token pair, and each reproduces independently in isolation: pub field (line 3, expected=189), let _ wildcard (expected=131 actual=123), tuple destructure (expected=131 actual=174 then 145/123), struct destructure (expected=145 actual=176), if-let (expected=184 actual=123), ?T option shorthand (expected=183/184). Removing one feature does not affect the others. These are separate, unimplemented grammar productions in the parser — not one underlying cause manifesting many ways. The bucket's own likely_fix ("Each is a small independent grammar production; batch low-cost ones together") explicitly concedes multiple independent causes. The bucket is a correctly-categorized GROUPING of independent one-off parse gaps, not a single-root-cause defect. Caveat: ~ bitwise-not produced only 1 error with a different shape and ?T produced a large cascade (12 errors) — consistent with each being its own distinct gap rather than a shared mechanism.

Minimal repro /tmp/verify_parse_gap_15.sio (kernel fn with `&![f64]` slice arg + `with GPU`) → mc.elf --check prints "Parse failed for module 0: 1 errors" / "error: parse_failed" / "parser reported 1 syntax errors", matching the bucket's claimed parser rejection. Component isolation pins a SINGLE cause: (a) `kernel fn k(n:i64) with GPU {}` alone → SAME parse_failed; (b) plain `fn k(n:i64, a:&![f64]) {}` (slice arg, no kernel) → PARSES fine, only type-check fails (semantic, not parse); (c) plain `fn k(n:i64) with GPU {}` → parses fine. So the parse rejection is triggered by the `kernel` keyword/item form, NOT by `&![f64]` slices nor `with GPU` (both already parse on a normal fn). The three named samples (kernel_fn_basic, gpu_vec_add, gpu_vec_scale) all reproduce the same parse_failed signature; gpu_vec_scale reports 2 errors because it has 2 `kernel fn` items — error count scales 1-per-kernel-fn-item, consistent with one missing grammar production. Bucket's likely_fix (add `kernel fn` to item grammar reusing normal fn-decl path) is the correct single fix; the `&![T]` slice claim in the description is already-parseable and not an independent cause.
